content: Finally note that the GAN architecture has two differences with basic copy-marked: (a) a distinct encoder for real and pseudo-sentence; (b) a different training regime for these encoders. To sort out the effects of (a) and (b), we reproduce the GAN setup with BT sentences, instead of copies. Using a separate encoder for the pseudo-source in the backtrans-nmt setup can be detrimental to performance (see Table TABREF32 ): translation degrades in French for all metrics. Adding GANs on top of the pseudo-encoder was not able to make up for the degradation observed in French, but allowed the German system to slightly outperform backtrans-nmt. Even though this setup is unrealistic and overly costly, it shows that GANs are actually helping even good systems.
